response: LedgerLite is a digital-bank REST API I built with Java 21 and Spring Boot. It handles authentication with JWTs, account opening, deposits and withdrawals, and transfers with pessimistic row locking and idempotency keys to prevent double-processing. It's covered by 14 automated tests, including integration tests against a real PostgreSQL container with Testcontainers, and it's deployed on a local Kubernetes cluster.

Nik-Blog is my personal portfolio and blog, built as a real multi-layer application: a Node.js/Express REST API with JWT auth in HTTP-only cookies, a Next.js 16 frontend with Server Components, and a private admin panel. It has a GitHub-sync job, a Notes module with Markdown content, and S3 image uploads behind a least-privilege IAM user. The S3/IAM infrastructure is managed with Terraform via terraform import, verified with zero drift against production.

nikblog-mcp is a real MCP (Model Context Protocol) server I built using the official MCP SDK. It exposes my portfolio as three callable tools and is deployed live on Render over streamable-HTTP, secured with bearer-token authentication using a timing-attack-safe comparison. I verified it end-to-end with a real client, not just a local test.

career-watch-mcp is a second, more advanced MCP server with real write operations enforced by a Pydantic schema, designed to be usable by multiple AI agents at once. I connected it to both Claude and Google Gemini (via Antigravity) and verified a real, unscripted session where Gemini used its own search grounding and recorded honest match scores.

nikblog-image-mcp is a third MCP server that closes a real manual workflow: generating and publishing cover images for my portfolio. It has two server-enforced safety gates, an overwrite guard and a two-step confirmation gate, and I caught a real bug before it could do damage by reading the backend code first and discovering the update endpoints fully replace a row instead of patching it.

instruction: What is the Code Review Agent project?
response: Code Review Agent is a LangChain tool-calling agent that reviews Python files using real, deterministic tools instead of model guesswork: a ruff linter wrapper and a hand-written ast-based docstring checker. The agent calls both tools, then prioritizes and explains the findings rather than dumping raw output.

SmartStock is a cloud-native AI inventory management platform for restaurants, built as a team of 5 for my PRJ666 industry capstone, graded A+. My role was Data Scientist and AI Engineer: I built a two-level NLP chat assistant, a RandomForest demand-forecasting pipeline, and a waste-log audit system, plus JWT auth and RBAC.

Fragments is a production-grade cloud-native REST microservice built with Express 5, handling 11 content types with on-the-fly conversion. It's deployed on AWS EC2/ECR with S3 and DynamoDB storage, has dual authentication (Cognito JWT in prod, HTTP Basic in dev), and full CI/CD with 64 Jest unit tests and 9 Hurl integration tests at about 89% line coverage.

leet-journal is my real DSA/LeetCode problem-solving practice in Python, documented as an actual journey rather than polished final solutions. It has one file per problem and one note per pattern recording the real bugs I hit while solving, not a rewritten clean version.

instruction: What AI frameworks do you have hands-on experience with?

instruction: What programming languages are you confident in?
